description: Given a string s, rearrange the characters so that no two adjacent characters are the same. If not possible, return an empty string.
intuition: Place the most frequent character first to maximize spacing between repeats. Use a max-heap to always pick the most frequent remaining character, but never pick the same one twice in a row by holding the last-used character aside for one round.
approach: Always place the most frequent available character, holding the previous character aside to avoid adjacent duplicates. Python selects from a heap; JavaScript sorts the candidate array before selecting. Return the previous character to the candidates after placing a different one.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: s = "aab"

Step 1: Count frequencies
  charCount = { a:2, b:1 }
  maxCount = 2, ceil(3/2) = 2 → feasible

Step 2: Build heap
  heap = [[-2,"a"], [-1,"b"]] (sorted by count ascending)

Iteration 1:
  Extract [-2,"a"], place "a"
  prevCount=0, no previous char to push back
  prevCount=-2+1=-1, prevChar="a"
  result=["a"], heap=[[-1,"b"]]

Iteration 2:
  Extract [-1,"b"], place "b"
  prevCount=-1 < 0, push [-1,"a"] back to heap
  prevCount=-1+1=0, prevChar="b"
  result=["a","b"], heap=[[-1,"a"]]

Iteration 3:
  Extract [-1,"a"], place "a"
  prevCount=0, no previous char to push back
  result=["a","b","a"]

Return "aba"
explanation:
1. If any character appears more than (n+1)/2 times, it's impossible.
2. Select the most frequent available character using the heap in Python or the sorted candidates in JavaScript.
3. After placing a character, hold it aside and push back the previous one.
4. This ensures no two adjacent characters are the same.
hints: If any character count exceeds (n+1)/2, it is impossible.
Use a max-heap to always place the most frequent character.
Hold the last placed character aside to prevent adjacency.
